attribution.note: Marcus's own sentence on his Substack. 'Same thing' carries forward his own claim that the H200 move is hardly popular with either party.

semantics.note: 'Hardly popular with either party' is a little softer than 'unpopular with both parties', but the meaning is close enough. It is an unhedged present-tense observation about the preemption proposal.

contract.note: Reading the claim as substantial opposition among officials in both parties is a fair, ordinary reading of 'hardly popular'. It does not require unanimity or a majority of voters. The inferred window of Nov 1 to Dec 9, 2025 is reasonable. The result depends on choosing officials over voters.

evidence.note: Signed letter dated Nov 25, 2025 in which 36 state attorneys general oppose a moratorium on state AI laws. This is substantial collective opposition from officials within the window.

The NY AG's official summary of the same letter calls the 36-member coalition bipartisan and ties it to the NDAA preemption language. Party labels are the office's own description, but it is an official record.

Dec 8, 2025 report. A Republican governor (DeSantis) opposes preemption and calls it unpopular, while Trump pushes for it. This shows Republicans are split, not broadly accepting, so it is context for both sides.

reviews.rationale: Within the window, a bipartisan coalition of 36 state attorneys general formally opposed broad preemption of state AI laws, and a prominent Republican governor also objected. That meets the support condition of substantial opposition in both parties. Trump's backing shows the Republican side was divided, but the evidence does not show broad acceptance within either party. This holds under the contract's fair reading that the claim is about officials.
